title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 130 (Re-opening of accounts on court's or Tribunal's orders)

content.overview: A company shall not re-open its books of account and shall not recast its financial statements unless an application in this regard is made by the Central Government, the Income-tax authorities, the Securities and Exchange Board, any other statutory regulatory body or authority or any person concerned and an order is made by a court of competent jurisdiction or the Tribunal to the effect that the relevant earlier accounts were prepared in a fraudulent manner or the affairs of the company were mismanaged during the relevant period casting a doubt on the reliability of financial statements.
content.glance: Re-opening of books or recasting of financial statements requires an order of a court or the Tribunal on the statutory grounds; voluntary board restatement is not enough under this section.
content.study:
## Section 130 — Re-opening of accounts

**No voluntary re-opening under this section.** Books of account shall not be re-opened and financial statements shall not be recast unless:
1. an application is made by the Central Government, Income-tax authorities, SEBI, any other statutory regulatory body or authority, or any person concerned; and
2. a court of competent jurisdiction or the Tribunal orders that the earlier accounts were prepared in a fraudulent manner, or the affairs were mismanaged during the relevant period casting doubt on reliability.

The order states the period for which books are re-opened and gives notice to the relevant authorities.

**Distinguish section 131.** Voluntary revision of financial statements or Board's report (for non-compliance with section 129 or 134) is under section 131, after Tribunal approval.

This note is a focused study aid; the topic remains under source and current-law review.

examples.title: No board-only re-opening
examples.body: Board cannot unilaterally re-open books under section 130; a court or Tribunal order on the stated grounds is required. Educational illustration.

hypotheticals.question: Can the board re-open accounts under section 130 without a court or Tribunal order?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 130 requires an order of a court or the Tribunal on the statutory grounds. Voluntary revision is a different route under section 131.

misconceptions.correction: Section 130 requires a court or Tribunal order on the stated grounds. Section 131 is the voluntary revision route.

questionsAndAnswers.question: When may a company re-open its books under section 130?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Only on an order of a court or the Tribunal, on application by the specified authorities or person concerned, where accounts were prepared fraudulently or affairs were mismanaged casting doubt on reliability.
